stacks.title: Explore → Plan → Write
stacks.pattern: Grok 4.7 explores cheap → Opus 5.5 plans → Grok/Astra stress-test → Grok writes
stacks.why: Keeps spend low on exploration; puts the strongest planner on architecture; uses Grok where $/token matters for volume.

stacks.title: Daily driver agent
stacks.pattern: Grok Bot for knowledge-work loops; Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 when the task is hard reasoning
stacks.why: @AlexFinn still treats Grok Bot as a knowledge worker, not a personal agent. Musk now says Bot will call the best backend, including Opus 5.5.

stacks.title: Cost ladder
stacks.pattern: Luna / Flash for fan-out → Sol, Sonnet 5.5, or Grok 4.7 for mid → Opus / Astra / Fable / Argon for apex
stacks.why: Match model tier to sub-task value. Parallel cheap agents, expensive models only on the critical path.

frontier.name: Claude Opus 5.5
frontier.note: AA Intelligence Index lead (max effort). $4/$20, cache reads $0.20. Strong on HLE, SciCode, Terminal-Bench ~60%. 1M context.

frontier.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
frontier.note: Mid-tier that sits near Opus on AA (56). Practitioner default for daily work; often ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol (52) at the same list price.

frontier.name: Claude Fable 5.1
frontier.note: Premium long-horizon tier. Still ahead of Grok 4.7 on vendor CursorBench (51.8% vs 46.3%) and Terminal-Bench; AA composite below Opus 5.5.

frontier.name: GPT-6 Astra
frontier.note: OpenAI flagship. AA 53 at max, level with Fable 5.1. Fewer output tokens per index task than peers. Long-context surcharge above 272k.

frontier.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
frontier.note: Current Sol line after the Sep 22 GPT-6 Sol ($2/$10, AA ~level with 5.6). Reported AA 52. Workhorse under a stronger planner.

frontier.name: GPT-6 Luna
frontier.note: Cheap fan-out tier. AA cost per index task ~$0.07 at max. No published flagship index score.

frontier.name: Gemini 4 Argon
frontier.note: AA 53 at high, level with Astra. Intro 50% off list $4/$20; cost/task ~$1.99 while promo holds, ~$3.98 after. 1M context. Public access not fully dated.

frontier.name: Grok 4.7
frontier.note: Flagship. Price/performance, not AA peak. Vendor wins on EEBench and some cyber/repo benches; trails on Terminal-Bench and the AA composite.

briefs.title: Grok Bot will call rival models
points: Musk (Oct 7): SpaceX will use the best backend per Grok Bot task, including Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, Suno, and other leading APIs. Outcome over house model.
That is a product change, not a new Grok weight. grok-4.7 API price is still $2/$6 (≤200k; $4/$12 above). Independent AA Intelligence Index still ~46 vs Opus 5.5 at 58.
Distribution the same day: SpaceXAI says Grok 4.7 is live on Microsoft Foundry, after Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Oct 1) and Bedrock.
Desktop stable is 0.66.0 (Oct 2), up from 0.63.0: voice memos, MCP/plugin import, 1Password, cloud agents, team-bot access lists. Changelog: x.ai/changelog/bot.
Frontier map unchanged at the top: Opus 5.5 AA 58 ($4/$20); Sonnet 5.5 AA 56 ($2/$10, Sep 28); Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon all AA 53. Argon intro price $2/$10, list $4/$20.
GPT-6.1 Sol (late Sep) is the current Sol at $2/$10, reported AA 52. Luna stays the cheap fan-out at $0.10/$0.50.
@AlexFinn (Oct 6): Grok Bot is his knowledge worker, not his personal agent (Hark/Muse for personal). Opus 5.5 remains the model he points at for serious vibe-coding sessions.
Vendor-side Grok claims to keep separate from AA: Musk on AA cyber index #1 (xHigh, Sep 30) and a quoted VulcanBench Frontier v4 sweep (Oct 6). Specialist benches, not the composite.
Roadmap clock is still the Sep 24 line: cautiously optimistic of a Fable/GPT-6 level model in 2–3 months (late Nov–late Dec). No name, no ship date.
briefs.assumption: Routing to Opus is announced, not measured. Which tasks leave Grok 4.7, and whether the user pays Opus rates, is not in the post. Until a named successor ships, treat Grok as the value model inside a multi-model Bot, not the AA leader.

briefs.title: Frontier map: Grok 4.7 vs Opus 5.5, Fable, GPT-6
points: Grok 4.7 remains SpaceXAI flagship (Sep 21): $2/$6, 500k context, coding + knowledge work focus.
Independent AA Intelligence Index: Grok 4.7 ≈ 46 vs Claude Opus 5.5 ≈ 58 and Fable 5.1 / GPT-6 Astra ≈ 53 — mid-pack on the composite, not the peak.
Vendor tables: Grok leads EEBench (64%) and Harvey Legal (19.6%); trails Fable on CursorBench (46.3% vs 51.8%) and Terminal-Bench (~38% vs ~56–58%).
Claude Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) is the current independent composite leader at lower $ than Fable ($4/$20 vs $10/$50) with strong agentic coding scores.
OpenAI GPT-6 line: Astra (Sep 3, flagship), Sol ($2/$10) and Luna ($0.10/$0.50) on Sep 22 for cost tiers under the same generation.
Grok Bot: ~418k weekly users reported mid-September (one month after Aug 11 beta) — product traction, not just model scores.
GitHub Copilot weekly (Sep 25): added Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol/Luna, and Grok 4.7 — multi-model is the default product posture.
X practitioners: multi-model stacks (Grok explore/write + Opus plan) and latency tests (Opus fastest, Grok slowest in one head-to-head) matter more than a single leaderboard row.
@AlexFinn: strong on Grok 4.7 + Grok Bot workflows; also heavy Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 daily-driver takes — useful counterweight to pure benchmarks.
Musk still owns the only first-party next-Grok date: cautiously optimistic Fable/GPT-6 level in 2–3 months (from Sep 24).
briefs.assumption: Expect SpaceXAI to optimize the next ship for Terminal-Bench / long-horizon agents and AA composite, not only price. Until then Grok is a strong value/coding option inside multi-model setups, not the solo AA #1.

briefs.title: Grok 4.7 ships — value, not AA peak
points: Same $2/$6 as 4.6; larger base; longer RL on multi-hour tasks; new safeguards.
Terminal-Bench roughly doubled vs 4.6 but still well behind Fable/Astra/Opus tier.
Independent AA Index ~46; critics call mid-pack vs 53–58 frontier; defenders stress $/task and specialist wins.
Available in Cursor, Grok Build, API, routers, clouds.
